title: Harvey's Elementary Grammar and Composition
sourceTitle: Harvey's Language Course: Elementary Grammar and Composition, Revised Edition
author: Thomas W. Harvey
licenseEvidence: Title page of the Internet Archive scan of the Library of Congress copy (elementarygramma00harv): 'Copyright, 1880, by Van Antwerp, Bragg & Co.' (first edition entered 1869). Published before 1930, so public domain in the USA; Library of Congress notes no known copyright restrictions.
description: Thomas Harvey's classic 1880 grammar, a favorite of 19th-century schoolrooms, for grades 4–7. Each day introduces one idea through a short question-and-answer talk, then the child makes sentences, corrects common mistakes, analyzes and diagrams, and writes compositions from pictures and plans. The full scanned book is free online.
includes: 97 lessons covering all 134 sections and the appendix in 14 units
Part I: the parts of speech, sentence-making, and picture compositions
Part II: parsing, sentence diagrams, rules of syntax, and letter writing
Answers for grammar and usage questions
A link to the exact page of the free scanned book for every lesson

lessons.title: Sections 1–2: Objects and Definitions
steps: Name the five senses and something you perceive with each
Read the definitions of object, word, language, and grammar
Answer the book's questions aloud, then copy the definition of grammar
questions: How many senses do we have?
Is joy something we perceive or something we are conscious of?
What does English grammar teach?
answers: How to speak and write the English language correctly

lessons.title: Sections 3–4: The Sentence; Declarative and Interrogative Sentences
steps: Make three sentences about a piece of chalk (or another object) the way the book does
Learn the five directions for writing sentences
Unscramble the word groups into telling sentences and asking sentences
questions: What is a group of words making complete sense called?
What mark ends a question?
Which kind of sentence states a fact?
lessons.notes: Keep making new scrambled sentences until fifteen-word sentences come easily, as the book suggests.

lessons.title: Section 4 (II): Imperative and Exclamatory Sentences
steps: Read how commands, entreaties, and exclamations are made
Unscramble the imperative and exclamatory word groups
Name the kind of each sentence in the book's list, then find each kind in your reader
questions: What kind of sentence is "Go to your seats, boys."?
What kind of sentence is "Oh, how pretty she is!"?
What mark usually follows an exclamatory sentence?

lessons.title: Sections 5–6: Quotation Marks; Parts of Speech
steps: Read when quotation marks are used and when they are not
Copy the four practice sentences, adding quotation marks and capitals
Talk through "Good scholars study diligently": which word names, tells what is done, describes, tells how
questions: Should quotation marks be used when we give someone's exact words?
What are the classes of words called?
How do we decide which class a word belongs to?

units.title: Part I: The Noun and the Simple Sentence (Sections 7–14)

lessons.title: Section 7: The Noun — Common and Proper
steps: Read the oral lesson on nouns, answering the questions aloud
Write five kinds of fruit, five rivers, five schoolmates, and so on from the book's list
Sort the word list into common and proper nouns, then parse two nouns using the model
questions: Is "volcano" a common or a proper noun?
Is "Lake Erie" a common or a proper noun?
What kind of letter begins a proper noun?

lessons.title: Section 8: Number
steps: Read how singular and plural nouns differ
Go over the ways of forming plurals (s, es, ves, ies, and words alike in both numbers)
Write the plurals of the thirty nouns in the list
questions: What is the plural of "knife"?
What is the plural of "folly"?
What is the plural of "sheep"?
lessons.notes: The book says plurals are learned by writing them, not by memorizing many rules; help with the hard ones.

lessons.title: Section 9: Abbreviations
steps: Read how abbreviations are made and punctuated
Copy the tables of abbreviations with what they stand for
Rewrite the practice sentences using abbreviations, and write the abbreviations for the days of the week
questions: What does "P. S." stand for?
What mark follows an abbreviation?
What is the abbreviation for Captain?

lessons.title: Sections 10–11: Contractions; Elements of a Sentence
steps: Tell which letters are left out in each contraction in the exercise
Learn the meanings of subject, predicate, and copula
Point out the subject, predicate, and copula in each practice sentence
questions: What mark shows that letters are left out of a word?
In "Iron is heavy," what is the subject?
In "Iron is heavy," what is the copula?

lessons.title: Section 12: The Predicate
steps: Read how quality-words and nouns can be predicates
Affirm a quality of each subject in the first list (e.g. "Oranges are yellow")
Give each listed quality a fitting subject, and state the class of each noun in the last list
questions: In "Horses are animals," what does the predicate tell?
Give a quality you could affirm of lead.
Is "animals" in "Horses are animals" a noun or a quality-word?
answers: The kind or class horses belong to
Any fitting quality, e.g. "Lead is heavy"

lessons.title: Section 13: Elements and Analysis
steps: Learn what elements, principal elements, and analysis are
Analyze "Iron is heavy" aloud following the model, and look at its line diagram
Analyze the nine practice sentences and diagram three of them
questions: What are the two principal elements of a sentence?
Is the copula called an element?
What is analysis?
answers: Separating a sentence into its elements

lessons.title: Section 14: Composition — Picture Lessons
steps: Look at the bird's-nest picture and answer its questions aloud, beginning "I see"
Write the answers as a short composition and read it back
Do the same with the dog-and-rats picture
questions: How should the first answer in a picture lesson begin?
Name one harm that rats do.
answers: Any fair answer, e.g. they eat or spoil grain and food
lessons.notes: Use other pictures too; the book recommends this exercise for several years.

lessons.title: Section 15: The Verb
steps: Read the oral lesson and learn the definition of a verb
Write a sentence using each verb in the list as a predicate ("Birds sing")
Point out the verbs in a page of your reader
questions: What does a verb usually express?
In "Fishes swim," which word is the verb?
Does "stand" in "Houses stand" show action or state?

lessons.title: Section 16: Classes of Verbs
steps: Learn transitive, intransitive, and copulative verbs and the objective element
Write seven sentences of each kind, and sentences using the listed nouns as objects
Analyze and diagram the ten practice sentences, then classify the verbs in the second list
questions: In "Cats catch mice," what is the objective element?
Is "grows" in "Corn grows" transitive or intransitive?
What kind of verb is "are" in "Lambs are playful"?

lessons.title: Section 17: Incorrect Language
steps: Read the five cautions about saw/seen, went/gone, did/done, came/come, was/were
Say each faulty example correctly aloud
Write the corrected sentences
questions: Correct: "I have saw a fine horse."
Correct: "He done his work well."
Correct: "You was there."
answers: I have seen a fine horse.

lessons.title: Section 18: Sentence-Making — Words in a Series
steps: Learn the two comma rules for words of the same kind used together
Arrange the word groups into sentences with correct commas
Fill the blanks in the nine exercises
questions: How many words of the same kind in a row need commas between them?
Punctuate: "Mary Susan and Ada are cousins."
answers: Mary, Susan, and Ada are cousins.

lessons.title: Section 19: Composition — Picture Lesson
steps: Talk about the picture of the children: names, ages, where they are
Choose one of the story ideas (playing shop, a day in the country, an afternoon alone)
Write the story and read it aloud
questions: What should every sentence of your story begin with?

units.title: Part I: Adjective, Article, and Participle (Sections 20–27)

lessons.title: Section 20: The Adjective
steps: Learn the difference between descriptive and definitive adjectives
Place each listed adjective before a noun and say which kind it is
Point out the adjectives in the nine sentences using the model
questions: Is "fearful" in "fearful storms" descriptive or definitive?
Is "these" descriptive or definitive?
Should "Spanish" begin with a capital?

lessons.title: Section 21: The Article
steps: Learn the definite and indefinite articles and when to use a or an
Put a or an before each word in the list and say why
Fill in the articles in the practice sentences
questions: Which article goes before "hour"?
Which article goes before "eagle"?
Which is the definite article?

lessons.title: Section 22: Sentence-Making with Adjectives
steps: Build sentences from the word groups, adding words where needed
Fill the blanks thoughtfully
Punctuate the sentences in Part II, noticing when two adjectives need no comma
questions: Does "a little old man" need a comma between "little" and "old"?
Punctuate: "Mary is a gentle sensible and well-behaved girl."
answers: Mary is a gentle, sensible, and well-behaved girl.

lessons.title: Sections 23–24: Incorrect Language; Composition — What I See
steps: Read the three cautions about a/an, these/those, and them/this here
Correct the faulty examples aloud
Describe what can be seen from your doorway or window and something that happens while you watch
questions: Correct: "I don't like these kind of apples."
Correct: "Henry is a honest lad."
Correct: "Look at them tramps."
answers: I don't like this kind of apples.

lessons.title: Section 25: The Participle
steps: Read the oral lesson on "James saw the man plowing"
Learn the present, perfect, and compound participles
Point out the participles in the exercises using the models
questions: What does every present participle end in?
Which participle is "having written"?
Name the participle in "The boy, laughing, ran away."

lessons.title: Section 26: The Participial Noun
steps: Read how a word like "skating" can be the name of an action
Point out the participial nouns using the model
Sort the words in the last exercise into participles and participial nouns
questions: In "I like skating," what part of speech is "skating"?
In "Miss Gray teaches writing," is "writing" a participle or a participial noun?

lessons.title: Section 27: Composition — An Outing
steps: Talk about the picture: where have the children been?
Write about a drive, a picnic, or a fishing trip
Underline two participles in your composition
questions: Name a participle you used in your story.
lessons.notes: Any correct -ing or -ed participle used as a modifier counts.

units.title: Part I: The Pronoun and Its Elements (Sections 28–35)

lessons.title: Sections 28–29 (I): The Pronoun; the Adjective Element
steps: Read why "John put John's hat on John's head" sounds wrong
Point out the pronouns in the practice sentences
Write five sentences with descriptive and five with definitive adjective elements
questions: What is a pronoun?
In "Small lakes are abundant," what is the adjective element?
answers: A word used instead of a noun

lessons.title: Section 29 (II): Possessives
steps: Learn what a possessive is and how the apostrophe is used
Write five sentences whose subjects are modified by possessives
Correct the faulty possessives in the last exercise
questions: Write the possessive of "children".
Correct: "The canary is not in it's cage."
What mark shows that a noun is a possessive?
answers: The canary is not in its cage.

lessons.title: Section 29 (III): Appositives
steps: Learn what an appositive is and when it is set off by commas
Write five sentences using appositives
Point out the appositives, then analyze the model sentences
questions: Find the appositive: "Whang, the Chinese miller, acted foolishly."
Does an unmodified appositive like "Milton the poet" need a comma?

lessons.title: Section 30: Personal Pronouns
steps: Learn first, second, and third person
Point out the personal pronouns in the practice sentences
Write five sentences each with personal pronouns as subjects, objects, and possessives
questions: What person denotes the speaker?
What person is "they"?
In "Henry admires them," how is "them" used?

lessons.title: Section 31: Possessive Pronouns
steps: Read how "ours" stands for both owner and thing owned
Write five sentences using possessive pronouns as subjects and five as predicates
Point out the possessive pronouns using the model
questions: Name the possessive pronoun in "That desk is mine."
Name three other possessive pronouns.
answers: Any three of: thine, his, hers, ours, yours, theirs

lessons.title: Section 32: Relative Pronouns and Clauses
steps: Learn what a clause, a relative pronoun, and an antecedent are
Point out the relative pronouns and their antecedents using the model
Say the compound forms made with -ever and -soever
questions: In "A man who is industrious will prosper," what is the relative pronoun?
What is its antecedent?
Make a compound relative from "who."

lessons.title: Section 33: The Relative Clause
steps: Write five sentences with relative clauses modifying subjects and five modifying objects
Analyze the model sentences
Change relative clauses to adjectives and adjectives to relative clauses
questions: Change to an adjective: "I have an apple that is rotten."
Change to a relative clause: "Industrious people always prosper."
answers: People who are industrious always prosper.

lessons.title: Section 34: Interrogative Pronouns
steps: Learn the interrogative pronouns and interrogative adjectives
Point out the interrogative pronouns using the model
Analyze the sentences, finding all the other parts of speech too
questions: Name the three interrogative pronouns.
In "Which book is yours?" is "which" a pronoun or an interrogative adjective?

lessons.title: Section 35: Incorrect Language — Pronouns
steps: Read the four cautions on pronouns
Correct each faulty example aloud
Write three corrected sentences from memory
questions: Correct: "Him and me were in the boat."
Correct: "Is that book your'n?"
Should "which" be used for persons?
answers: He and I were in the boat.

units.title: Part I: Adverb, Preposition, and Phrase (Sections 36–42)

lessons.title: Section 36: The Adverb
steps: Read the oral lesson on "Birds sing sweetly"
Point out the adverbs in the practice sentences using the model
Write sentences with adverbs modifying verbs, adjectives, and other adverbs
questions: In "The wind blew furiously," which word is the adverb?
What does "very" modify in "Very loud reports were heard"?

lessons.title: Sections 37–38: The Adverbial Element; the Adverbial Clause
steps: Learn what an adverbial element and an adverbial clause are
Point out the adverbial clauses in the practice sentences
Analyze "He trembles when it thunders" and three more sentences
questions: In "Flowers bloom when spring comes," what is the adverbial clause?
What question does that clause answer?

lessons.title: Section 39: Incorrect Language — Adverbs
steps: Read the three cautions on double negatives and adjectives/adverbs
Correct the faulty examples aloud
Write the corrected sentences
questions: Correct: "I don't want nothing today."
Correct: "Samuel speaks very distinct."
Correct: "This flower smells sweetly."

lessons.title: Section 40: Composition — The Lion
steps: Read the description of the lion three or four times
Close the book and write it from memory
Compare with the book and fix any spelling or punctuation
questions: Does the lioness have a mane?
Where does the lion most often hide to catch his prey?
Does a lion often attack people?
answers: Near a spring or a river
Rarely, unless wounded or very hungry

lessons.title: Section 41: The Preposition
steps: Read the oral lesson on "A man of wealth rode by our house"
Learn what a preposition and its object are, and say the list of common prepositions
Point out the prepositions in the practice sentences using the model
questions: In "He came from France to America," name the prepositions.
What is the object of "to"?

lessons.title: Section 42 (I): The Phrase
steps: Learn what a phrase is and how phrases act as adjectives or adverbs
Analyze "Habits of industry will lead to prosperity" using the model
Change phrases to single words and clauses, as in "with care" = "carefully"
questions: Change the phrase to one word: "Henry studies with care."
Is "of industry" an adjective or an adverbial phrase?

lessons.title: Section 42 (II): The Infinitive; Position of Modifiers
steps: Learn what an infinitive is and its sign "to"
Analyze "To love is to obey" and the other models
Learn the rule for placing modifiers, then fix the badly placed modifiers in the exercise
questions: What is the sign of the infinitive?
Where should a modifying word, phrase, or clause be placed?
answers: As near the word it modifies as possible

units.title: Part I: Conjunction, Interjection, and Kinds of Sentences (Sections 43–48)

lessons.title: Section 43: The Conjunction
steps: Read the oral lesson on "Ellen and Mary study botany"
Learn the definition of a conjunction and how it differs from a preposition
Point out the conjunctions in the practice sentences
questions: In "Eli and Silas will improve, if they study," name the conjunctions.
Does a conjunction have an object as a preposition does?

lessons.title: Section 44: Compound Elements
steps: Learn what a compound element is and how to punctuate it
Write five sentences each with a compound subject, predicate, object, adjective, and adverb
Analyze the model sentences
questions: What is the compound subject in "Ellen and Lucy are my sisters"?
Punctuate: "We run jump and talk at recess."
answers: We run, jump, and talk at recess.

lessons.title: Sections 45–46: Simple and Compound Sentences
steps: Learn the simple sentence and the compound sentence and its members
Combine short sentences into one, and change compound sentences to simple ones
Analyze "The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament showeth his handiwork"
questions: How many propositions does a simple sentence have?
What are the parts of a compound sentence called?
Is "Wheat grows in the field, and men reap it" simple or compound?

lessons.title: Section 47 (I): Complex Sentences
steps: Learn complex sentence, principal clause, and subordinate clause
Study the models for complete analysis
Write five sentences each with clauses as subjects, objects, adjectives, and adverbs
questions: In "I know where gold is found," which is the principal clause?
Which is the subordinate clause?

lessons.title: Section 47 (II): Reducing Complex Sentences
steps: Read how a clause can be shortened to a phrase or a word
Reduce the complex sentences to simple ones
Expand the simple sentences into complex ones
questions: Reduce: "A man who is wealthy lives there."
Reduce: "We started when the sun rose."
answers: A wealthy man (or a man of wealth) lives there.

lessons.title: Section 48: The Interjection
steps: Read the oral lesson on "Hurra! we have found him"
Point out the interjections using the model
Name every part of speech in two of the sentences
questions: In "Hush! they are coming," what is the interjection?
What mark usually follows an interjection?

units.title: Part II: The Noun in Full (Sections 49–59)

lessons.title: Sections 49–51: Properties of the Noun; Gender; Person
steps: Learn the four properties of the noun and the four genders
Tell the gender of each noun in the list
Write sentences using nouns of the first, second, and third person
questions: What gender is "parent"?
What gender is "cart"?
What is the feminine of "duke"?

lessons.title: Sections 52–53: Number; Formation of the Plural
steps: Review the rules for forming plurals
Write the plurals of the words, letters, and signs in the list
Write the singulars of the plural list
questions: What is the plural of "calf"?
What is the plural of "brother-in-law"?
What is the singular of "phenomena"?

lessons.title: Sections 54–55: Case; Declension
steps: Learn the four cases: nominative, possessive, objective, absolute
Decline two nouns in both numbers following the book's table
Tell the case of each noun in a few sentences of your reader
questions: What case is "James" in "James, bring me a book"?
What case is "buffaloes" in "Indians hunt buffaloes"?
What case is "Ray's" in "Ray's Algebra"?

lessons.title: Sections 56–58: Parsing Nouns
steps: Learn what parsing is and the order of parsing a noun
Parse the nouns in the models aloud
Analyze the practice sentences, parse the nouns, and correct the faulty plurals
questions: Correct: "Three chimnies were on fire."
In "Borneo is a large island," what case is "island"?

lessons.title: Section 59: Composition — Animals
steps: Read the plan for describing a squirrel (size, form, color, food, habits)
Write a description of the squirrel following the plan
Describe another animal with the general plan, then parse its nouns
questions: Name three topics from the general plan for describing an animal.
answers: Any three of: size, form, color, food, habits, disposition, where found, uses

units.title: Part II: The Pronoun in Full (Sections 60–76)

lessons.title: Sections 60–62: Personal Pronouns and Their Declension
steps: Learn the simple and compound personal pronouns
Read the remarks on "you," "we," and "it"
Decline I, thou, he, she, and it in both numbers
questions: What is the objective case of "she"?
What is the possessive plural of "I"?
How is a compound personal pronoun formed?

lessons.title: Sections 63–64: Parsing Personal Pronouns
steps: Learn the order of parsing a personal pronoun
Parse the pronouns in "I see them on their winding way"
Analyze the practice sentences, then write two sentences about the eagle and parse their pronouns
questions: In "You and he are my friends," what case is "he"?
What case is "my"?
lessons.notes: Finish the eagle composition as a second sitting if time runs short.

lessons.title: Sections 65–67: Possessive Pronouns
steps: Learn the possessive pronouns and the emphatic "my own"
Study both methods of parsing "That house is mine, not yours"
Analyze the practice sentences and parse the possessive pronouns
questions: Name the possessive pronouns.
Find the possessive pronoun: "This sled is not yours."
answers: mine, thine, his, hers, ours, yours, theirs

lessons.title: Sections 68–71: Relative Pronouns
steps: Learn the simple and compound relatives, and when "that" and "as" are relatives
Decline who, which, and what
Parse the relatives in the models, then write about the quail and parse its pronouns
questions: Name the four simple relative pronouns.
What is the possessive form of "who"?
What is the objective form of "who"?

lessons.title: Sections 72–74: Interrogative Pronouns
steps: Learn the interrogative pronouns and the meaning of "subsequent"
Parse "Who invented gunpowder?" following the model
Parse the interrogatives in the practice sentences
questions: What is the subsequent of an interrogative pronoun?
With what must an interrogative agree in gender, person, and number?
answers: The part of the answer it stands for

lessons.title: Sections 75–76: False Syntax — Pronoun Cautions
steps: Learn what false syntax means
Read the five cautions on pronouns
Correct the faulty sentences aloud and in writing
questions: Correct: "Who did you see?"
Which comes first, the second person or the first?
Correct: "John he went home."

units.title: Part II: The Adjective in Full (Sections 77–82)

lessons.title: Section 77: Descriptive Adjectives and Comparison
steps: Learn the positive, comparative, and superlative degrees
Compare adjectives with -er/-est and with more/most
Compare the irregular adjectives (good, bad, little, many)
questions: Compare "good."
Which degree is used when comparing two things?
Compare "beautiful."

lessons.title: Section 78: Definitive Adjectives
steps: Learn pronominal adjectives: demonstratives, distributives, indefinites
Learn the numeral adjectives: cardinal, ordinal, and multiplicative
Find a definitive adjective of each kind in your reader
questions: Is "each" a demonstrative or a distributive?
Is "third" a cardinal or an ordinal?
Name two demonstratives.
answers: Any two of: this, that, these, those, former, latter, both, same, yon, yonder

lessons.title: Sections 79–80: Parsing Adjectives
steps: Learn the order of parsing an adjective and Rule XII
Parse the adjectives in the models
Analyze the practice sentences and parse every adjective
questions: To what does an adjective belong, according to Rule XII?
Parse "fearful" in "Fearful storms sweep over these islands" briefly.
answers: An adjective; descriptive; positive degree; belongs to "storms"

lessons.title: Sections 81–82: Adjective Cautions; Composition — Plants
steps: Read the four cautions and correct the examples
Follow the plan to write about the peach tree
Choose another plant and describe it with the general plan
questions: Correct: "This is the most wisest plan."
Correct: "the two first chapters."

units.title: Part II: The Verb in Full (Sections 83–100)

lessons.title: Sections 83–84: Properties of the Verb; Voice
steps: Learn the five properties of the verb
Learn active and passive voice and how the passive is formed
Change active sentences to passive and back
questions: Change to the passive: "The boy wrote a letter."
Which voice shows the subject acting?
answers: The letter was written by the boy.

lessons.title: Section 85: Mode
steps: Learn the five modes with an example of each
Tell the mode of each verb in the practice sentences
Write a description of the oak and name the modes of its verbs
questions: How many modes are there?
What mode is "Go"?
What mode is "If he were here"?

lessons.title: Section 86: Tense
steps: Learn the six tenses with an example of each
Make a sentence in each tense with the verb "write"
Tell the tense of each verb in the exercise
questions: How many tenses are there?
What tense is "I had written"?
What tense is "I shall have written"?

lessons.title: Section 87: Signs of the Tenses
steps: Study the table of tense signs in the active voice
Write the verb "walk" in every tense of the indicative
Write a description of the pine, then name the modes and tenses of its verbs
questions: What is the sign of the present perfect tense?
What is the sign of the future tense?

lessons.title: Sections 88–89: Person and Number of Verbs; Auxiliaries
steps: Learn how a verb agrees with its subject in person and number
Learn the auxiliary verbs
Say the present tense of "to write" in all persons and numbers
questions: Correct: "He write well."
Name three auxiliary verbs.
answers: Any three of: do, be, have, shall, will, may, can, must, might, could, would, should

lessons.title: Sections 90–91: Conjugation; the Verb "To Be"
steps: Learn what conjugation and principal parts are
Read through the conjugation of "to be"
Write a synopsis of "to be" in the first person singular
questions: Give the principal parts of "be."
What is the past indicative of "be" with "we"?

lessons.title: Section 92: Conjugation of "To Love" (Active Voice)
steps: Read the active conjugation of "to love" in all modes
Recite the indicative mode aloud
Write a synopsis of "to love" in the first person singular, active voice
questions: Give the principal parts of "love."
Give the present perfect, first person singular.

lessons.title: Section 93: Synopsis of "To Love" (Passive Voice)
steps: Read the passive synopsis of "to love"
Write the passive synopsis in the third person singular
Compare the active and passive forms side by side
questions: Give the past tense passive, first person singular.
Give the future tense passive, first person singular.

lessons.title: Section 94: Coordinate Forms of Conjugation
steps: Learn the progressive, emphatic, and interrogative forms
Write a synopsis of some of the listed verbs (think, teach, see)
Describe a currant bush and parse its verbs
questions: Which form is "He was writing"?
Which form is "I do write"?
Which form is "Did he write?"

lessons.title: Sections 95–96: Regular, Irregular, Defective, and Redundant Verbs
steps: Learn regular and irregular verbs
Learn defective and redundant verbs
Give the principal parts of ten verbs and say which are irregular
questions: Is "go" regular or irregular?
Give the principal parts of "write."
Is "must" a defective verb?

lessons.title: Sections 97–98: Parsing Verbs
steps: Learn the order of parsing a verb
Parse "Liberty is sweet" and the other models aloud
Analyze the practice sentences and parse the verbs
questions: Parse "is" in "Liberty is sweet" briefly.
answers: A verb; irregular (be, was, been); copulative; indicative mode, present tense; third person singular, agreeing with "liberty"

lessons.title: Section 99: Composition — Sugar
steps: Read the description of sugar several times and write it from memory
Describe tapping maple trees and making maple sugar
Write two sentences on "Lazy Boys" and parse the verbs
questions: From what plant is most sugar made?
What is the part of the syrup that will not crystallize called?
From what root is sugar made in France?

lessons.title: Section 100: False Syntax — Verb Cautions
steps: Read the six cautions on verbs
Correct the faulty examples aloud
Write the corrected sentences
questions: Correct: "He said that the earth was round." (general truth)
Correct: "I seen him yesterday."
Correct: "It ain't mine."
answers: He said that the earth is round.

units.title: Part II: Adverb, Preposition, Conjunction, Interjection (Sections 101–116)

lessons.title: Sections 101–102: Classes and Comparison of Adverbs
steps: Learn the five classes of adverbs and the questions they answer
Learn adverbial phrases and conjunctive adverbs
Compare adverbs such as soon, well, and wisely
questions: What class of adverb answers "How?"
What class is "seldom"?
Compare "well."

lessons.title: Sections 103–105: Parsing Adverbs; Composition — The Apple
steps: Parse "bravely" in "The soldiers fought bravely" by the order of parsing
Write a description of an apple following the plan
Describe another product with the general plan
questions: What does an adverb modify, according to Rule XVII?

lessons.title: Sections 106–108: The Preposition in Full
steps: Read about relations between objects and how prepositions show them
Parse the prepositions in the models
Write two sentences describing spruce gum and parse the prepositions
questions: In "They went aboard the ship," what is the object of the preposition?
What case is the object of a preposition in?

lessons.title: Sections 109–111: The Conjunction in Full
steps: Learn coordinate and subordinate conjunctions and correlatives
Parse the conjunctions in the models
Find and classify the conjunctions in the practice sentences
questions: Into what two classes are conjunctions divided?
Is "and" coordinate or subordinate?
Is "if" coordinate or subordinate?

lessons.title: Section 112: Composition — Iron
steps: Read the description of iron several times
Write it from memory
Underline the conjunctions in your composition
questions: What is iron made into that is next in hardness to the diamond?
What is iron called after it is drawn off from the blast furnace?
What is melting ore in a blast furnace called?

lessons.title: Sections 113–115: The Interjection in Full
steps: Learn the definition of an interjection and its rule
Parse "Eh! are you sure of it?" following the model
Write five sentences with interjections and punctuate them
questions: Do interjections depend on other words in the sentence?

lessons.title: Section 116: Composition — Lead
steps: Follow the plan to write a description of lead
Describe another substance (salt, coal, copper...) with the general plan
Read your description aloud and fix the punctuation
questions: Name three topics from the general plan for describing a substance.
answers: Any three of: properties, where found, what it is found with, how obtained, uses

units.title: Part II: Ellipsis, Syntax, and Letter Writing (Sections 117–123)

lessons.title: Section 117: Ellipsis
steps: Learn what ellipsis is and what "understood" means
Go through the ten kinds of words that may be left out
Supply the missing words in the practice sentences
questions: What is understood in "Come"?
Supply the missing word: "He gave me an orange."
answers: to ("He gave to me an orange")

lessons.title: Section 118: Abridgment
steps: Learn how a clause is abridged to an infinitive, participial noun, or participle
Analyze the models
Abridge the complex sentences in the exercise
questions: Abridge: "I knew that it was he."
Abridge: "The fair was not held, because the weather was unfavorable."
answers: I knew it to be him.
The weather being unfavorable, the fair was not held.

lessons.title: Section 119: Modified Subject and Predicate
steps: Learn grammatical and logical subject and predicate
Point them out in the practice sentences
Analyze three sentences fully
questions: In "The tall old tree fell," what is the grammatical subject?
What is the logical subject?

lessons.title: Section 120: Composition — A Hurricane
steps: Read the description of a West Indies hurricane several times and write it from memory
Follow the plan to describe an earthquake
Describe another event of nature (a thunderstorm, a flood) with the general plan
questions: What happens to the barometer before the hurricane?
Where do sea-birds fly during the storm?

lessons.title: Section 121 (I): Rules of Syntax I–X
steps: Learn what syntax and a rule of syntax are
Read Rules I–X on cases and pronoun agreement
Find an example of each rule in your reader
questions: In what case is the subject of a proposition?
In what case is the object of a preposition?
Must a pronoun agree with its antecedent?
answers: Yes, in gender, person, and number

lessons.title: Section 121 (II): Rules of Syntax XI–XX
steps: Read Rules XI–XX on verbs, modifiers, and connectives
Correct sentences that break the agreement rules
Parse a sentence from your reader, giving a rule for every word
questions: Correct: "John and James was there."
Correct: "Either John or James are to blame."
answers: Either John or James is to blame.

lessons.title: Section 122 (I): Letter Writing — The Parts of a Letter
steps: Read the oral lesson about the envelope and the letter
Label the date, address, body, and signature on the model letter
Address an envelope correctly
questions: Where does the stamp go on the envelope?
What is the part of a letter giving the place and day called?

lessons.title: Section 122 (II): Writing a Letter
steps: Review the model letter
Write a letter telling what you plan to do next Saturday afternoon
Fold it and address an envelope for it
questions: Name two closing words you could use before your signature.
answers: Any two, e.g. Yours truly, Yours faithfully, Very respectfully

lessons.title: Section 123 (I): Miscellaneous Exercises 1–14
steps: Analyze sentences 1–7 aloud
Parse the words of sentences 8–14
Copy one sentence you like
questions: In "Still waters are commonly deepest," what degree is "deepest"?
In "She saw a glory in each cloud," what is the object of "saw"?

lessons.title: Section 123 (II): Miscellaneous Exercises 15–31
steps: Read the poetry extracts aloud
Analyze three of them
Memorize one short extract
questions: In "Labor is life!" what kind of sentence is it?

lessons.title: Sections 124–125 (I): Punctuation; the Comma, Rules I–VI
steps: Learn what punctuation is
Read comma Rules I–VI with their examples
Copy and punctuate a few sentences that use these rules
questions: What does a comma denote?
Punctuate: "Reading writing and arithmetic are taught here."
answers: Reading, writing, and arithmetic are taught here.

lessons.title: Section 125 (II): The Comma, Rules VII–XII
steps: Read comma Rules VII–XII
Punctuate sentences with direct address, appositives, and quotations
Write one sentence for each rule
questions: Punctuate: "James bring me a book."
Punctuate: Quoth the raven "Nevermore."

lessons.title: Sections 126–128: The Semicolon, the Colon, and the Period
steps: Read the rules for the semicolon, the colon, and the period
Find each mark in your reader and say which rule it follows
Write a sentence that needs a semicolon
questions: Which shows greater separation, a semicolon or a comma?
Which mark shows the greatest degree of separation?
What mark goes after every abbreviated word?

lessons.title: Sections 129–131: Interrogation Point, Exclamation Point, and Dash
steps: Read the rules for the question mark, the exclamation point, and the dash
Punctuate the practice sentences
Write a sentence that breaks off suddenly, using a dash
questions: What does the exclamation point show?
When is a dash used?
answers: Where a sentence breaks off abruptly or changes its meaning suddenly

lessons.title: Sections 132–134: Curves, Brackets, and Other Marks
steps: Read about curves (parentheses) and brackets
Learn the other marks: apostrophe, hyphen, quotation marks, and the rest
Answer the closing questions on punctuation aloud
questions: What do curves enclose?
What does an apostrophe show?
answers: Words that could be left out without hurting the sense
That letters are left out, or possession

lessons.title: Appendix: Irregular Verbs
steps: Read down the table of irregular verbs, saying the three principal parts
Quiz each other on twenty of them
Write sentences using the past and perfect participle of five verbs
questions: Give the principal parts of "begin."
Give the principal parts of "freeze."
Give the principal parts of "swim."

lessons.title: Appendix: Unipersonal Verbs; Capital Letters, Italics
steps: Read about unipersonal verbs ("It rains")
Learn the rules for capital letters
Copy a paragraph and check every capital by the rules
questions: Should the first word of every line of poetry begin with a capital?
Is "It snows" an example of a unipersonal verb?
In handwriting, how do you show that a word should be in italics?
